summary: Replace the accessory serpentine belt that drives the alternator, water pump, power steering, and AC compressor.
steps: 1. Note belt routing before removal (photo it) or check the routing diagram sticker under the hood. 2. Use a breaker bar or belt tensioner tool on the tensioner pulley bolt to release belt tension. 3. Slip belt off the pulleys, starting with the easiest to reach. 4. Inspect tensioner and idler pulleys for play or noise, replace if rough. 5. Route new belt per diagram, last pulley is usually the alternator or AC compressor. 6. Release tensioner slowly, confirm belt seats in all pulley grooves.
torque_specs: Tensioner pulley mounting bolt: verify against RealOEM or dealer spec for your exact engine revision before using a memorized number
part_numbers: Serpentine belt and tensioner/idler pulleys: verify exact OEM part numbers against RealOEM.com using your VIN, revisions exist across production years
tools_needed: Tensioner release tool or long breaker bar, flashlight
notes_warnings: Double check routing before removing the old belt, a mis-routed belt can cause the AC compressor or alternator to spin backward. Replace tensioner and idler pulleys at the same time if they have any play, they're cheap compared to a belt failure on the road.

summary: Replace a failed or failing alternator.
steps: 1. Disconnect negative battery terminal first. 2. Remove serpentine belt (see serpentine belt procedure). 3. Disconnect electrical connector and B+ terminal nut from the alternator, note orientation. 4. Remove alternator mounting bolts. 5. Maneuver alternator out, it can be tight depending on what else is in the way on this engine bay. 6. Install new/rebuilt alternator in reverse order, torque mounting bolts and B+ terminal nut to spec. 7. Reinstall belt, reconnect battery, verify charging voltage with engine running.
torque_specs: Alternator mounting bolts and B+ terminal nut: verify against RealOEM or dealer spec before using a memorized number
part_numbers: Alternator: verify exact OEM part number against RealOEM.com using your VIN, and confirm whether yours has an integrated voltage regulator before ordering a replacement
tools_needed: Socket set, possibly need to loosen other components for clearance depending on engine bay layout
notes_warnings: Always disconnect the battery first, this is a live electrical component. Double check the B+ terminal nut is torqued properly, a loose one can arc and melt the connector. If charging voltage still looks wrong after replacement, check the battery and wiring before assuming the new alternator is also bad.

summary: Drain and replace coolant, or replace the radiator if it's failed.
steps: 1. Let engine cool completely before opening any part of the cooling system. 2. Remove engine undertray if present. 3. Open radiator drain petcock (or disconnect lower hose) into a drain pan, loosen expansion tank cap to help it drain. 4. If replacing the radiator, disconnect upper/lower hoses, electric fan connector, and remove radiator mounting. 5. Install new radiator if applicable, reconnect hoses and fan. 6. Refill with BMW-spec coolant mixed to the correct ratio, do not use a generic universal coolant. 7. Bleed the system per BMW's bleed procedure, this engine needs air purged properly or it will run hot. 8. Run engine to operating temperature with heater on full, check for leaks, top off after cooling.
torque_specs: Radiator mounting and hose clamp fasteners: verify against RealOEM or dealer spec before using a memorized number
part_numbers: Radiator, coolant (BMW-spec blue antifreeze, correct for this generation), thermostat and water pump if doing those at the same time since labor overlaps: verify exact OEM part numbers against RealOEM.com using your VIN
tools_needed: Drain pan, BMW-spec coolant, possibly a cooling system bleed/fill tool for a cleaner bleed
notes_warnings: This is the big one on N52-family engines: the electric water pump and plastic thermostat housing are known weak points, if you're already in here for a coolant change and either one is original, strongly consider replacing them proactively rather than coming back in a year. Never use non-BMW-spec coolant, the wrong chemistry attacks the plastic components in this cooling system.
